method: Same five frozen HN threads, 233 Luna-low candidates, frozen production core and consolidation settings as consolidation-matched-eight-v1; only the model differs. Isolated sequential consolidation calls, model order rotating by thread. The same two-pass Luna-low scoring at concurrency 10. One Sonnet 5 medium-effort review per thread sees only the 2 added anonymous variants, with each thread's common exclusion list from the matched review supplied as fixed.
limitations: The added models are graded in a separate review call from the matched eight. The candidate denominator is identical, but the reviewer sees different companion outputs, which can shift grades.
Five threads, one accepted output per model per thread; model judgments, not calibrated accuracy.
The Sonnet reviewer shares a provider/model family with Opus 5.5.
Prices come from a later catalog snapshot than the matched experiment; costs use uncached token prices.

consolidationIssues.explanation: Candidate 22's claim about shutting down Nitter infrastructure in favor of alternatives is a policy question distinct from candidates 26/28's personal-boycott question; a commenter can consistently hold one pole of 22 while holding either pole of 26/28, so these are independently holdable claims merged into a single axis.

Candidate 10 (should users go elsewhere due to restrictions) and candidate 19 (does old Reddit allow anonymous access in all contexts) are separable: one can believe login is sometimes required (19B) yet still find Reddit usable overall (10B), so forcing them into one two-pole axis manufactures a correlation not guaranteed by the source candidates.

Candidate 30 is a normative claim about where links should point, while candidate 1 is a factual/empirical claim about whether Nitter links eventually break; a commenter could prefer primary links for ethical reasons regardless of link durability, or believe proxy links stay usable while still preferring primary links, so these are not necessarily the same disagreement.
